name: Product Spec (PM-led PRD)
description: A product manager writes a detailed, build-ready PRD — fed by parallel user research and an engineering feasibility read, then sharpened by a sprint-scoping pass. Use this when you already know you want the thing and need the spec engineers can build against. Fan-in on the PM, then a scoping refinement. All roles pinned to product/engineering agents; brain chains remain editable in the UI.

steps.title: User & problem research: {{idea}}
steps.description: Research the users and the real problem behind "{{idea}}": who has this problem, how they solve it today, the top 3 unmet needs, and the 5-8 concrete user stories that matter most. Cite evidence or clearly mark assumptions. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Engineering feasibility read: {{idea}}
steps.description: Give a fast engineering feasibility read on "{{idea}}": the core components, the hardest technical risk, external dependencies/APIs required, a rough effort tier (S/M/L) per component, and anything that would materially change scope. Output as markdown.

steps.title: Write the PRD: {{idea}}
steps.description: You are the Product Manager. Using the user research and the engineering feasibility read provided, write the detailed PRD for "{{idea}}": problem statement, target users & prioritized user stories, MVP scope with an explicit OUT-of-scope list, functional + non-functional requirements, success metrics & instrumentation, key edge cases, dependencies, and open questions with owners. Be diplomatically ruthless about focus. Output the full PRD as markdown.

steps.title: Scope into a shippable first sprint: {{idea}}
steps.description: Take the PRD provided and cut it into a shippable first sprint for "{{idea}}": the smallest slice that delivers real user value, an ordered backlog of tickets each with a one-line acceptance criterion, the explicit cut list (what's deferred and why), and the top risk to the sprint. Output as markdown.
